external_entities.name: Developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and can manually start a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand.

processes.name: Build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces container images, publishes them, and invokes deployment.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.

processes.name: Deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release for the estate and responds to release queries from store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: Store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office that polls for the current release, pulls changed images, and restarts the till container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 stores, each with a small server.

processes.name: Till software
processes.description: Till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: Git server
data_stores.description: Self-hosted repository server containing developer branches and the main branch.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_stores.name: Image registry
data_stores.description: Registry holding the finished container images tagged with commit SHA values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: Release record
data_stores.description: The record held by the deploy controller identifying which image SHA the estate should use.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on

data_stores.name: Dependency lockfile
data_stores.description: The dependency lockfile used during dependency resolution.
data_stores.notes: The lockfile is taken as given.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developer pushes branch contents to the Git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: start build
data_flows.description: A merge to main starts a build picked up by the build runner.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the Git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reads the dependency lockfile while resolving dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: resolves the dependency lockfile

data_flows.name: download dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches the public package registry to download dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: publish image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: Finished container image tagged with commit SHA

data_flows.name: update release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The call uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: Image SHA and shared build token

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: read release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the registry when its running image differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the Git server and deploy controller run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: Build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: Store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of store back-office servers running the till software.

trust_boundaries.name: Internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet location of the public package registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The build runner presents a non-web interface because it is described as a build job and accepts build triggers rather than serving a web application.
assumptions.basis: The text describes the build runner as picking up merges, resolving dependencies, producing images, and accepting manual rebuilds.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller presents a non-web interface because it is described as a controller called by pipeline and store-server processes.
assumptions.basis: The text describes the runner calling the controller and store servers asking it for the current release.

assumptions.assumption: The store server presents a non-web interface because it is described as a polling server process that pulls images and restarts a container.
assumptions.basis: The text describes the store server's polling and image-pull behavior, not a web application interface.

assumptions.assumption: The dependency lockfile contains business-critical build data, so the build runner's interaction with it carries business-critical-data.
assumptions.basis: The text identifies it as the lockfile used to resolve dependencies in the build pipeline.

assumptions.assumption: The public package registry is an external system because it is described as a public registry on the internet outside the pipeline's stated environments.
assumptions.basis: The text says dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet.
